hints: Notice that $X$ points up and to the right while $Y$ points down and to the right, so compare their horizontal and vertical parts separately.
Recall that vector addition adds like components, and that $X-Y$ means $X+(-Y)$ where $-Y$ points up and to the left.
Check what happens to the vertical parts when you add $X$ and $Y$, and what happens to the horizontal parts when you add $X$ and $-Y$.
walkthrough: Split each vector into horizontal and vertical parts. $X$ has right plus up, and $Y$ has right plus down with similar sizes in the diagram.
For $X+Y$, add the parts head-to-tail. The rightward parts add together, while the up part of $X$ and the down part of $Y$ cancel, leaving a resultant pointing to the right.
For $X-Y$, rewrite it as $X+(-Y)$. Reversing $Y$ gives $-Y$ pointing up and to the left.
Now add $X$ to $-Y$. The rightward part of $X$ and the leftward part of $-Y$ cancel, while the up part of $X$ and the up part of $-Y$ add together.
The $X-Y$ resultant therefore points vertically upward. Right for $X+Y$ with up for $X-Y$ is option B. This is option B.

options.A: Right is correct for $X+Y$, but down is opposite to $X-Y$ because subtracting $Y$ reverses its downward component to upward.
options.B: Right follows from adding two rightward horizontal components, and up follows from $X- Y$ adding two upward vertical components.
options.C: Left is wrong for $X+Y$ because both $X$ and $Y$ have components to the right, and down is wrong for $X-Y$.
options.D: Up is correct for $X-Y$, but left is wrong for $X+Y$ because the horizontal components reinforce to the right.
